strategy.summary: Three tests named in SYNC-21 pass and fail on the same commit. A probe with retries off and shuffled order (as CI runs it: `vitest run --sequence.shuffle`) reproduced all three: retry 9/10, subscribers 6/10, saveAll 6/10. Two causes are in the tests and get fixed there, keeping every assertion. The third is a real ordering bug in src/bulk.js, so that test gets quarantined and reported.
inScope: test/retry.test.js › retry › retries a failed call after a back-off
test/subscribers.test.js › subscribers › stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes
test/bulk.test.js › saveAll › resolves with the ids in the order of the records
outOfScope: Changing application code in src/ (bulk.js ordering bug is reported, not fixed)
assumptions: CI runs the suite with --sequence.shuffle (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so test order within a file varies per run
Vitest isolates modules per test file, so the subscribers module-level Map is shared only between tests within test/subscribers.test.js
Existing tests change only where the cause is; every assertion and case stays

risks.description: Quarantining saveAll's ordering test leaves the documented contract of saveAll (ids in record order) unchecked until the app is fixed
risks.mitigation: Defect recorded and a GitHub issue filed with the cause (src/bulk.js pushes ids in completion order); the skip comment names it so it is un-skipped with the fix

acceptanceCriteria.text: retry › retries a failed call after a back-off passes on every run, still proving the task is called a second time after a back-off and the result resolves to 'ok'
subscribers › stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes passes on every run in any test order, still proving publish reaches 0 handlers and the handler isn't called
saveAll resolves with the ids in the order of the records (src/bulk.js doc comment), whatever order the saves complete in

testCases.title: retries a failed call after a back-off
steps: Mock task rejecting once then resolving 'ok'
Wait with vi.waitFor until the task has been called 2 times
testCases.expected: task called twice; result resolves 'ok'; passes 20/20
testCases.rationale: Cause: the test sleeps a fixed 40ms, but retry's back-off is retryDelay(0) = 20ms + Math.floor(Math.random()*40) jitter, i.e. 20–59ms, so whenever the jitter exceeds ~20ms the second call hasn't happened yet ('expected 2 times, got 1'). Fix: wait for the condition (vi.waitFor on the call count) instead of a fixed delay.

testCases.title: stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes
steps: Subscribe a handler to 'records' and call the returned stop
Assert 0 handlers reached and handler not called
testCases.expected: publish returns 0, handler not called, in any shuffled order; passes 20/20 with shuffle
testCases.rationale: Cause: order dependence via shared module state. src/subscribers.js keeps one process-wide handlers Map; 'tells every handler subscribed to the topic' subscribes two handlers to 'records' and never unsubscribes, so when CI's shuffle runs it first, this test's publish reaches 2 ('expected 2 to be +0', only under certain seeds). Fix: every test removes the subscriptions it makes (onTestFinished with the returned stop), so no test leaks handlers to another.

testCases.title: resolves with the ids in the order of the records
testCases.expected: Currently fails ~40% ('expected [second, first]'); quarantined with it.skip and a comment until src/bulk.js is fixed
testCases.rationale: Cause is in application code: saveAll in src/bulk.js runs saves concurrently and does ids.push(await client.save(record)), so ids land in completion order; the records client's latency is random, so the second save often finishes first. The doc comment promises record order. A test change can't fix it without hiding the bug: quarantine (skip) with a comment, record the defect and file an issue.

strategy.environmentNotes: No services; pure unit tests run with `npx vitest run` (CI adds --sequence.shuffle).

defects.title: saveAll returns ids in save-completion order, not record order
defects.description: AC3: saveAll's doc comment (src/bulk.js) promises ids in the order of `records` so callers can pair them by index. It runs saves concurrently and does `ids.push(await client.save(record))` inside Promise.all's map, so each id is appended when its save resolves; with variable latency the second record's save often finishes first and its id comes first.
defects.evidence: probe_stability (10 shuffled runs, retries off): saveAll › resolves with the ids in the order of the records passed 6/10; 4× "AssertionError: expected [ 'second', 'first' ] to deeply equal [ 'first', 'second' ]" at test/bulk.test.js:10.
